description: M1 schema + migrations built from an empty DB: all 15 ordered .sql migrations (tables, enums/CHECKs, insert-only ledger trigger + REVOKE, deferred per-transfer balance CONSTRAINT TRIGGER, non-negative CHECK, UNIQUE(user_id,key), config table, all indexes from schema §6, and the system-account/risk-rule/config/job_locks seed), plus the seed script (1000 users / 2000 wallets / 100000 transfers via batch inserts) and the migrate-from-empty + immutability + constraints tests. Depends on FEAT-001 (migrate runner, db layer). Precedes all money-path work.
steps: Create migrations 0001_users.sql ... 0012_config.sql exactly per schema §2 columns and constraints: users(id IDENTITY PK, name, email UNIQUE, phone UNIQUE, kyc_status CHECK in pending|verified|rejected, created_at); accounts(id IDENTITY PK, user_id BIGINT NULL FK users, is_system BOOLEAN, system_type NULL CHECK in cash_in|cash_out|fee_revenue, currency CHECK='INR', balance BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at, CHECK account-kind coherence, CHECK(is_system OR balance>=0)); transfers(id PK, type CHECK in top_up|peer_transfer|withdrawal|reversal, status CHECK in PENDING|HELD|COMPLETED|REVERSED|FAILED, amount BIGINT CHECK(amount>0), from_account_id BIGINT NOT NULL FK accounts, to_account_id BIGINT NOT NULL FK accounts, note TEXT NULL, reverses_transfer_id BIGINT NULL self-FK, created_at); ledger_entries(id PK, transfer_id FK, account_id FK, direction CHECK in debit|credit, amount BIGINT CHECK(amount>0), created_at); idempotency_keys(id PK, user_id FK, key UUID, body_hash CHAR(64) NOT NULL, status CHECK in in_progress|completed, response_code INT NULL, response_body JSONB NULL, created_at, UNIQUE(user_id,key)); reconciliation_runs(id PK, started_at, finished_at NULL, status CHECK in running|ok|problems|error, global_ok BOOLEAN, problem_count INT, per-check counts); reconciliation_problems(id PK, run_id FK, check_name, entity_id BIGINT NULL, expected TEXT, actual TEXT, created_at); job_locks(job_name TEXT PK, locked_at NULL, locked_by NULL); risk_rules(id PK, rule_name UNIQUE, threshold BIGINT, window_seconds INT NULL, action CHECK in hold|flag, enabled BOOLEAN); risk_flags(id PK, transfer_id FK, rule_name, explanation TEXT NULL, label CHECK in likely_ok|review|likely_fraud NULL, created_at); audit_log(id PK, transfer_id FK ONLY, old_status TEXT NULL, new_status TEXT, actor TEXT, created_at) with NO FK to users; config(key TEXT PK, value TEXT NOT NULL). Use GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY for all surrogate PKs.

Create 0012_indexes.sql with every index from schema §6: ledger_entries(account_id, created_at DESC); ledger_entries(transfer_id); transfers(from_account_id, created_at DESC); transfers(to_account_id, created_at DESC); transfers(created_at DESC, id DESC); unique already on idempotency_keys(user_id,key); risk_flags(transfer_id); audit_log(transfer_id); reconciliation_problems(run_id).

Create 0013_ledger_insert_only_trigger.sql: a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger function on ledger_entries that RAISE EXCEPTION, plus REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON ledger_entries FROM the app role (document the role name; if running as a single role, REVOKE from PUBLIC/that role as design §7 states). The trigger blocks only UPDATE/DELETE, not INSERT, so seed INSERTs still work.

Create 0014_ledger_balanced_transfer_trigger.sql: CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ... AFTER INSERT ON ledger_entries DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION check_transfer_balanced(); the function re-aggregates SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE direction='debit') vs SUM(... 'credit') FROM ledger_entries WHERE transfer_id = NEW.transfer_id and RAISE EXCEPTION (SQLSTATE 23514-class) on mismatch. Deferred so transient imbalance between inserts is allowed; an unbalanced transfer can never COMMIT.

Create 0015_seed_system_accounts_and_rules.sql: insert the three system accounts (cash_in, cash_out, fee_revenue) each is_system=true, user_id NULL, balance=0, zero opening ledger_entries; insert risk_rules pinned per design §14/§20.3-H: single_over_max threshold=100000000 action='hold' enabled=true; velocity threshold=1000 window_seconds=60 action='hold' enabled=true; rapid_drain threshold=100000000 window_seconds=60 action='flag' enabled=true; insert config('fee_paise','0'); insert job_locks('reconciliation', NULL, NULL). This runs after the insert-only trigger (safe) and before any multi-entry transfer so the deferred balance trigger does not interfere.

Create scripts/seed.ts: insert 1000 users, 2000 wallets (2 per user), and 100000 peer_transfer rows with their balanced ledger_entries using BATCHED multi-row INSERTs (chunked, e.g. 1000 rows per statement) so it stays reasonably fast; keep balances consistent (seed opening top-ups so wallets can fund the transfers, or seed via cash_in). Make amounts/users deterministic enough to be reusable. This is the FR-17 seed, distinct from per-test seeding.

Create test/integration/migrate.test.ts (AC-15): run runMigrations against an empty test DB, assert all expected tables/triggers exist (query information_schema / pg_trigger), then re-run and assert it is a no-op (schema_migrations count unchanged, no error).

Create test/integration/ledgerImmutability.test.ts (AC-12): insert a balanced pair of ledger entries for a throwaway transfer, assert UPDATE and DELETE on ledger_entries both raise; and assert that attempting to COMMIT an unbalanced per-transfer entry set (a debit with no matching credit) raises at COMMIT via the deferred trigger.
Create test/integration/constraints.test.ts (AC-13): assert driving a non-system wallet negative violates CHECK(is_system OR balance>=0); assert a system account may go negative.
acceptance_criteria: npx tsc --noEmit passes (seed.ts and any TS compiles).
Running migrations against an EMPTY Postgres 15 builds the full schema with zero errors and is a no-op on second run (AC-15).
ledger_entries UPDATE/DELETE raise, and an unbalanced per-transfer entry set cannot COMMIT (AC-12).
Non-system wallet cannot go negative; system account can (AC-13).
scripts/seed.ts inserts 1000 users / 2000 wallets / 100000 transfers via batched inserts without constraint violations.
verification: If a real Postgres is reachable (DATABASE_URL set): npm run migrate against an empty DB -> exit 0; run again -> no-op. Then npx vitest run test/integration/migrate.test.ts test/integration/ledgerImmutability.test.ts test/integration/constraints.test.ts -> pass.
If no Postgres is available in-environment: record in findings that schema/trigger/constraint tests were authored but NOT executed, and why (no Postgres). Do NOT claim a pass.
findings:
COMPLETED (code+tests authored and typecheck-verified; Postgres-dependent apply/integration tests authored but NOT executed — see honesty note).

VERIFICATION RUN LOCALLY:
- `tsc --noEmit` -> EXIT 0, zero errors (includes seed.ts and all three integration tests).
- `vitest run` -> EXIT 0: 15 unit tests pass; the 8 integration tests (migrate 4, ledgerImmutability 2, constraints 2) SKIP automatically because DATABASE_URL is unset. Invoked via `node node_modules/.../tsc` and `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs` because PowerShell execution policy blocks the npx.ps1 shim.

HONESTY NOTE (no Postgres here): Docker and psql/postgres are NOT on PATH in this environment, so migrations were NEVER applied to a real DB and the three integration tests (migrate/immutability/constraints) were NEVER executed — only authored and typechecked. No Postgres pass is claimed. The integration suite is gated by `SKIP_INTEGRATION = !process.env.DATABASE_URL` in test/integration/helpers.ts (via `describe.skipIf(...)`), so CI with a real Postgres service + DATABASE_URL will run them; locally they no-op instead of failing.

MIGRATION ORDERING (follows authoritative design §5/§6, which supersedes the FEAT-002 step text that said '0012_config'): 0001_users, 0002_accounts, 0003_transfers, 0004_ledger_entries, 0005_idempotency_keys, 0006_reconciliation (both reconciliation_runs and reconciliation_problems), 0007_job_locks, 0008_risk_rules, 0009_risk_flags, 0010_audit_log, 0011_config, 0012_indexes, 0013_ledger_insert_only_trigger, 0014_ledger_balanced_transfer_trigger, 0015_seed_system_accounts_and_rules. All PKs are BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY. Runner applies migrations/*.sql lexicographically, one txn per file (FEAT-001 src/db/migrateRunner.ts).

NAMES LATER FEATs RELY ON:
- Tables: users, accounts, transfers, ledger_entries, idempotency_keys, reconciliation_runs, reconciliation_problems, job_locks, risk_rules, risk_flags, audit_log, config (+ schema_migrations from the runner).
- Key columns/enums (exact CHECK value sets):
  * users.kyc_status in (pending|verified|rejected), default 'pending'; email, phone are UNIQUE.
  * accounts(id, user_id NULL FK users, is_system BOOL, system_type NULL CHECK in cash_in|cash_out|fee_revenue, currency CHECK='INR' default 'INR', balance BIGINT NOT NULL default 0). Constraints: accounts_kind_coherence (system => user_id NULL & system_type set; wallet => user_id set & system_type NULL); accounts_non_negative CHECK (is_system OR balance>=0).
  * transfers(id, type CHECK in top_up|peer_transfer|withdrawal|reversal, status CHECK in PENDING|HELD|COMPLETED|REVERSED|FAILED, amount BIGINT CHECK(amount>0), from_account_id NOT NULL FK accounts, to_account_id NOT NULL FK accounts, note TEXT NULL, reverses_transfer_id NULL self-FK). No 'fee' type.
  * ledger_entries(id, transfer_id FK transfers, account_id FK accounts, direction CHECK in debit|credit, amount BIGINT CHECK(amount>0), created_at). INSERT-ONLY.
  * idempotency_keys(id, user_id FK users, key UUID, body_hash CHAR(64) NOT NULL, status CHECK in in_progress|completed, response_code INT NULL, response_body JSONB NULL). UNIQUE constraint name: idempotency_keys_user_key_unique UNIQUE(user_id,key).
  * reconciliation_runs(id, started_at, finished_at NULL, status CHECK in running|ok|problems|error, global_ok BOOLEAN NULL, problem_count INT default 0) PLUS per-check count columns: global_balance_count, per_transfer_balance_count, stored_vs_computed_count, negative_balance_count, orphan_count (all INT NOT NULL default 0). These map to design §13 checks (a)-(e); reconciliationService (later FEAT) must populate them.
  * reconciliation_problems(id, run_id FK, check_name TEXT, entity_id BIGINT NULL, expected TEXT NULL, actual TEXT NULL, created_at). Suggested check_name values (not DB-constrained): global_balance, per_transfer_balance, stored_vs_computed, negative_balance, orphan.
  * job_locks(job_name TEXT PK, locked_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL, locked_by TEXT NULL).
  * risk_rules(id, rule_name UNIQUE, threshold BIGINT, window_seconds INT NULL, action CHECK in hold|flag, enabled BOOLEAN default true).
  * risk_flags(id, transfer_id FK, rule_name TEXT, explanation TEXT NULL, label CHECK in likely_ok|review|likely_fraud NULL, created_at).
  * audit_log(id, transfer_id FK transfers ONLY, old_status TEXT NULL, new_status TEXT NOT NULL, actor TEXT NOT NULL, created_at). No FK to users.
  * config(key TEXT PK, value TEXT NOT NULL).
- Triggers/functions (0013/0014): function ledger_entries_block_mutation() + trigger ledger_entries_insert_only (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE, RAISE EXCEPTION message contains 'insert-only'); function check_transfer_balanced() + CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ledger_entries_balanced (AFTER INSERT DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED; RAISE EXCEPTION SQLSTATE 23514/check_violation, message contains 'unbalanced'). Plus REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON ledger_entries FROM PUBLIC. APP-ROLE NOTE: this exercise connects as a single Postgres role (the DATABASE_URL role), so there is no separate least-privilege app role; the REVOKE targets PUBLIC per design §7's single-role fallback, and the trigger is the owner-proof primary guard (an owner retains table privileges, so the REVOKE alone would not stop the owner — the trigger does).
- Indexes (0012): ledger_entries_account_created_idx (account_id, created_at DESC); ledger_entries_transfer_idx (transfer_id); transfers_from_account_created_idx; transfers_to_account_created_idx; transfers_created_id_idx (created_at DESC, id DESC); risk_flags_transfer_idx; audit_log_transfer_idx; reconciliation_problems_run_idx.
- SEED (0015, idempotent via ON CONFLICT): three system accounts (cash_in, cash_out, fee_revenue; is_system=true, user_id NULL, balance=0, zero opening ledger_entries); risk_rules PINNED per design §14/§20.3-H: single_over_max threshold=100000000 window_seconds=NULL action='hold' enabled=true; velocity threshold=1000 window_seconds=60 action='hold' enabled=true; rapid_drain threshold=100000000 window_seconds=60 action='flag' enabled=true; config('fee_paise','0'); job_locks('reconciliation', NULL, NULL).

SEED SCRIPT (scripts/seed.ts, run via `npm run seed`): calls runMigrations(pool) first, then in ONE transaction inserts 1000 users (emails seed.user.N@example.com, kyc verified), 2000 wallets (2 per user, balance starts 0), 2000 opening top_up transfers (cash_in -> each wallet, OPENING_BALANCE=100000000 paise) and 100000 peer_transfer rows (round-robin wallet[i]->wallet[i+1], 100 paise each), each with a balanced debit/credit ledger pair via chunked (1000-row) multi-row INSERTs; stored balances are computed in memory and written in a final bulk UPDATE so accounts.balance == credits-debits exactly (reconciliation check (c) clean on seeded data). cash_in is driven negative (allowed: system account). NOT executed here (no Postgres) but typechecks.

TESTS: test/integration/{migrate,ledgerImmutability,constraints}.test.ts + test/integration/helpers.ts (createTestPool + SKIP_INTEGRATION). migrate.test.ts asserts all expected tables exist (information_schema.tables), both ledger triggers exist (pg_trigger, non-internal), the seed rows exist, and a second runMigrations returns applied=[] with unchanged schema_migrations count. ledgerImmutability.test.ts inserts a balanced pair for a throwaway transfer between two system accounts and asserts UPDATE and DELETE both reject (/insert-only/i), and that a lone debit cannot COMMIT (/unbalanced/i via the deferred trigger). constraints.test.ts asserts driving a non-system wallet to -1 rejects (CHECK) and that cash_in may go to -500 (then restores to 0).

Git: committed on branch main; NO remote (never push/add remote).
